name: Tab completion as streamed multi-line edit prediction
what: The editor predicts the user's next edit, not just the next token: a suggestion can replace a whole range, span several lines and is accepted with Tab, shown either as ghost text or as an inline diff.
how: Client services cppService, cppEventLoggerService, cppTelemetryService, cppTypeService, cppDebouncingService and cppDiffingProviderBridgeService drive the flow. The request (aiserver.v1.StreamCppRequest) carries the current file, several encodings of recent edit history (diff_history strings, file_diff_histories with timestamps, merged_diff_histories, block_diff_patches), linter_errors, scored context_items, parameter_hints, lsp_contexts, lsp_suggested_items, additional_files, filesync_updates, cpp_intent_info, a control_token (QUIET, LOUD, OP) and client timing fields. The response streams text plus range_to_replace, begin_edit/done_edit markers, suggestion_confidence, model_info and a binding_id; the client consumes it through a buffered flushCpp loop. Backend entry points are AiService.StreamCpp and CppService.StreamHoldCpp.
verevonRelevance: Verevon is not an IDE, but the same pattern (send structured recent-edit history plus diagnostics, stream range replacements with a confidence score) would suit inline assist inside Verevon's document, sheet or code artifact editors.
notes: Quality 5 because: Broadest request contract seen for inline prediction (edit history, LSP, linter, delta sync) with streamed ranges and confidence; actual suggestion quality cannot be measured from the client. Evidence key: OUT = scratchpad/tmp/cursor/app/out (byte copy of install resources/app/out). MAIN = OUT/main.js; EXTH = OUT/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js; DESK = OUT/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js; GLASS = OUT/vs/workbench/workbench.glass.main.js. 'X#name' = a protobuf makeMessageType/makeEnum/service typeName or identifier searchable in that file; field lists were extracted with scratchpad/tmp/aif/msg.js, enum.js, svc3.js. BEAUT/<f>:<n> = line n of scratchpad/tmp/cursor-h/beaut/<f> (esbuild-beautified copies of extension bundles: exec_main.js = extensions/cursor-agent-exec/dist/main.js, host_main.js = cursor-agent-host/dist/main.js, mcp.js = cursor-mcp/dist/main.js, retrieval.js = cursor-retrieval/dist/main.js, shadow.js = cursor-shadow-workspace/dist/extension.js, alwayslocal.js = cursor-always-local/dist/main.js, commits.js = cursor-commits/dist/main.js, agentworker.js = cursor-agent-worker/dist/main.js, browserauto.js = cursor-browser-automation/dist/extension.js). RAW/NN = scratchpad/tmp/cursor_raw/NN_*.txt. APP = install resources/app. All bundle facts are on minified or beautified code: names, fields and strings are reliable, behaviour is inferred from them. Other keys: SCRATCH:/PATH: = under scratchpad/ (the audit scratch directory); REA:ev_... = REA evidence id (retained in the REA session; saved result files in scratchpad/tmp/cursor_raw and tmp/cursor-h); 'X#name' prefixes were verified by an automated script that searched all four bundles for each token. Ratings: quality is relative to the peer set and judged from client evidence only, with the reason given at the start of each record's notes.

name: Cursor prediction: jump to the next edit location
what: After an accept, undo or editor change the model also predicts where the user will want to edit next and offers to move the cursor there, so repeated edits chain with the Tab key.
how: AiService.StreamNextCursorPrediction and CursorPredictionService.CursorPredictionConfig supply models as {name, radius} pairs. CursorPrediction carries request_id, line_number and a source enum (ALWAYS_ON, ACCEPT, UNDO, EDITOR_CHANGE). StreamCppResponse can embed a cursor_prediction_target, and CppConfigResponse.is_fused_cursor_prediction_model signals that prediction is fused into the main Tab model. CppSessionEvent has accept, reject and suggest events specific to cursor predictions, so every jump is evaluated like an edit.
verevonRelevance: A 'where to look next' prediction is a transferable idea for Verevon's agent review screens (jump to the next changed cell, paragraph or file), but needs an edit-history signal Verevon does not collect today.
notes: Quality 4 because: A distinct next-edit jump with its own models and evaluation events; only contract-level evidence, no behaviour trace.

name: Server-driven Tab tuning and client-side suppression heuristics
what: The Tab experience is tuned remotely (context window size, debounce, ghost text vs diff) and low-value suggestions are suppressed on the client before the user sees them.
how: CppConfigResponse returns above_radius, below_radius, global and client debounce milliseconds, is_ghost_text, allows_tab_chunks, include_unchanged_lines, recently_rejected_edit_thresholds and max_number_of_cleared_suggestions_since_last_accept. A Heuristic enum lists six suppression rules: LOTS_OF_ADDED_TEXT, DUPLICATING_LINE_AFTER_SUGGESTION, DUPLICATING_MULTIPLE_LINES_AFTER_SUGGESTION, REVERTING_USER_CHANGE, OUTPUT_EXTENDS_BEYOND_RANGE_AND_IS_REPEATED and SUGGESTING_RECENTLY_REJECTED_EDIT. The client reads the config through CppConfig and refreshes tab context with RefreshTabContext.
verevonRelevance: Shipping a typed remote-config contract plus a named list of output-quality heuristics lets Verevon tune any inline suggestion surface without a client release.
notes: Quality 4 because: Typed remote config and a named list of suppression rules show mature iteration; the thresholds themselves are server-side.

name: Tab context: edit history, recently viewed files, LSP and delta file sync
what: Tab requests are small because the server mirrors open files and the client sends only deltas, while still enriching requests with language-server symbols, parameter hints, diagnostics and recently viewed files.
how: FileSyncService (FSUploadFile, FSSyncFile, FSConfig, FSGetFileContents, FSGetMultiFileContents) maintains a server-side copy; StreamCppRequest.filesync_updates carries deltas and CppConfigResponse.check_filesync_hash_percent and enable_filesync_debounce_skipping govern drift checks. AiService.CppEditHistoryAppend and CppEditHistoryStatus ship the edit log (EditHistoryAppendChangesRequest has a PrivacyModeStatus enum: PRIVACY_ENABLED, IMPLICIT_NO_PRIVACY, EXPLICIT_NO_PRIVACY). cppTypeService produces relevant LSP suggestions and parameter hints; CppConfigResponse carries enable_rvf_tracking, exclude_recently_viewed_files_patterns and an import_prediction_config.
verevonRelevance: For any Verevon surface that streams large working context to the model, server-side mirroring with delta updates and periodic hash checks cuts payload and latency.
notes: Quality 4 because: Delta file sync plus multi-source context is sophisticated, but depends on server-side mirroring that cannot be inspected.

name: Tab guardrails: secret files, disabled languages and hooks
what: Tab is never offered in .env-style files or in languages the user switched off, and enterprises can intercept what Tab reads and writes through hooks.
how: A client function (bGg) refuses plaintext files whose path ends in .env, .env.local, .env.production and eight similar variants, and any language listed in the cursor.cpp.disabledLanguages setting. The agent hook system includes the events beforeTabFileRead and afterTabFileEdit, so policy scripts see Tab traffic as well as agent traffic. Tab on/off is also gated by CppConfigResponse.is_on and should_let_user_enable_cpp_even_if_not_pro.
verevonRelevance: A built-in deny list for secret-bearing files in every AI context path (not only Tab) is a cheap safety default Verevon's file attach and workspace features should copy.
notes: Quality 4 because: Sensible secret-file and language denials plus hook coverage; the secret filename list is short and regex-free.

name: Tab fate tracking and evaluation loop
what: Every Tab suggestion is followed to its fate (accepted, rejected, partially accepted) and a very detailed editor event timeline is kept for model evaluation when privacy settings allow.
how: CppService.RecordCppFate, MarkCppForEval and AddTabRequestToEval feed an eval set; MarkCppRequest has labelled response types (GOOD, BAD, BAD_CONTEXT, BAD_REASONING, BAD_FORMATTING, BAD_RANGE, BAD_FALSE_POSITIVE_TRIGGER, BAD_FALSE_NEGATIVE_TRIGGER and others). CppSessionEvent bundles 40 event kinds (accept, reject, partial accept, linter error, cursor movement, scroll, copy, tab close, cmd-k, chat, search, terminal, git, worktree, browser, tool call). CppStoppedTrackingModelEvent records why tracking stopped (FILE_TOO_BIG, FILE_DISPOSED, CHANGE_TOO_BIG).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's answer feedback loop could log a similar per-turn 'fate' (accepted, edited, regenerated, abandoned) under the same privacy gates instead of only thumbs.
notes: Quality 4 because: Rich fate and labelled-eval plumbing; whether session events leave the machine under privacy modes is unverified. Whether session events are uploaded in privacy mode is not provable from the client; see the privacy records.

name: Cmd+K inline edit and terminal command generation
what: A selection-scoped inline prompt rewrites code in place with a streamed diff; the same pattern exists in the terminal to generate commands.
how: CmdKService offers StreamCmdK, StreamHypermode (a separate path with a selectable hyper_model), RerankCmdKContext, StreamTerminalCmdK, RerankTerminalCmdKContext and GetRelevantChunks. StreamCmdKRequest includes context_items, previous_edit(s) and upcoming_edits, images, links, diff_history, diff_to_base_branch and rules; the response streams edit_start, edit_stream, edit_end, chat and status_update. AiService adds StreamFullFileCmdK, BackgroundCmdK and StreamTerminalAutocomplete. A terminal AI-check setting (cursor.terminal.enableAiChecks) exists.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's document and artifact editors lack a selection-scoped 'edit this with a prompt' action (artifacts are read-only today); this is the interaction to emulate.
notes: Quality 4 because: Complete, long-established feature with a terminal variant; the pattern is common across IDE assistants.

name: Model-native edit tools chosen per vendor
what: The agent edits files with whichever edit tool format the underlying model was trained on: search-and-replace for Anthropic, Gemini and xAI models, an apply-patch format for OpenAI GPT-5 family and Cursor models.
how: A vendor switch builds the tool set: for anthropic, gemini, xai and unknown vendors it registers Write plus StrReplace; for openai and cursor vendors with isGpt5Family it registers ApplyPatch (a '*** Begin Patch' style parser with file-operation locks). The dedicated apply model of earlier versions has been reduced: FastApplyService now only exposes ReportEditFate and WarmApply. Edit errors are split into model-visible and client-visible messages.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's provider abstraction should let tool shape (patch vs string replace) vary by model family instead of one edit contract for every provider.
notes: Quality 4 because: Matching edit-tool format to model family is rare among peers; effect on edit success rates was not measurable here. The claim that no separate apply model remains in the agent edit path is INF from the reduced FastApplyService surface.

name: StrReplace engine with whitespace-tolerant matching and did-you-mean errors
what: Agent edits succeed even when the model's quoted text differs from the file by indentation or line endings, and failures return actionable hints instead of a bare error.
how: The engine finds exact matches first, then falls back to a line-by-line trimmed comparison (first line may end-match, last line may start-match) and normalises CRLF. It rejects empty old_string and identical old/new, requires replace_all for multiple matches, and builds a unified diff with context 3. Large edits (original plus new over 262144 characters) are diffed in a Piscina worker pool sized to half the cores.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's artifact update tools would benefit from tolerant matching and structured failure hints, which also reduce wasted tool-call turns.
notes: Quality 4 because: Tolerant matching, did-you-mean errors and worker-based diffing are solid engineering; the approach is otherwise common.

name: Shadow workspace: lint feedback on AI edits without touching the user's files
what: After the agent edits code, linter and compiler diagnostics for the change are fed back to the model from a hidden copy of the project, so the agent can fix its own errors without disturbing what the user sees.
how: A hidden window serves aiserver.v1.ShadowWorkspaceService (13 methods including GetLintsForChange, SwWriteTextFileWithLints, SwGetLinterErrors, SwCallClientSideV2Tool, SwGetMcpTools) over a local socket; the main window registers as client (registerShadowClientProvider / registerShadowServerProvider). The agent tool read_lints reads diagnostics, with a 10 s timeout. A setting cursor.general.enableShadowWorkspace controls it.
verevonRelevance: A 'verify in a throwaway copy' loop (render a draft artifact, run a validator) is a candidate for Verevon's Do mode before it presents changes.
notes: Quality 4 because: An isolated lint loop avoids disturbing the user's files; it adds hidden-window complexity. Transport detail (Unix socket or named pipe over Connect/HTTP1.1) is from the sibling harness notes and was spot-checked, not fully re-derived.

name: Codebase index: Merkle-tree sync, embeddings, similarity-based index reuse
what: The workspace is indexed for semantic search by uploading only changed files; a brand-new clone can reuse an existing teammate's index instead of re-embedding everything.
how: The retrieval extension builds a Merkle tree (native MerkleClient) over embeddable files, computes a SimHash similarity vector, then runs RepositoryService.FastRepoInitHandshakeV2 with doCopy:true so the server can copy a similar index (GetCopyStatus). It syncs mismatched subtrees (SyncMerkleSubtreeV2), uploads files (FastUpdateFileV2) and signals FastRepoSyncComplete. Defaults: 50 concurrent uploads, absolute cap 100,000 files, auto-index cap 10,000 files, re-index period 600 s, 2 MB batches. Admin blocklists, a global ignore list and a codebase_protection policy gate what is indexed.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Data Plane indexes server-side corpora; the Merkle-diff plus similarity-copy design is relevant if Verevon ever indexes user-local folders or git repos.
notes: Quality 5 because: Merkle sync, similarity-based index reuse, privacy-aware keys and admin controls make this the most complete retrieval pipeline observed.

name: Instant grep: Rust n-gram index with ripgrep fallback
what: Regex search across large repositories answers from a prebuilt n-gram index, falling back to ripgrep when the index cannot serve the query.
how: A native Rust tool (crepectl, crate crepe built on gix, regex-automata, rkyv, memmap2, rayon) builds index.bin, metadata.json and postings.bin per worktree and commit with a memory limit, using a sparse n-gram frequency table (string 'github-sparse-freq' in the binary). The TypeScript GrepClient queries it and records why it fell back (no_index, unsupported_shape, index_no_snapshot, index_busy, index_unavailable, exec_failure, timeout, no_overlap); a monitor raises an alert when most queries fall back in a window. It also serves VS Code's text search provider and pushes tracked git state (status, branch) into the request context.
verevonRelevance: A Rust-native, memory-bounded text index with an explicit fallback taxonomy is a good template for Verevon's Rust Model Plane tools that search workspaces or sandboxes.
notes: Quality 5 because: A native index with an explicit fallback taxonomy and a storm alert shows unusual engineering rigour for search. Crate list for crepectl comes from strings in the sibling scratch dump (tmp/cursor-h/crepectl.strings.txt), not re-extracted here. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): instant_grep_indexing off.

name: Semantic search tool, custom embeddings and reranking
what: Agents can search by meaning as well as by regex; results are chunked on syntax boundaries and reranked.
how: The agent tool SEMANTIC_SEARCH_FULL calls RepositoryService.SemSearch or SemSearchFast (server streaming). The embedding model enum lists VOYAGE_CODE_2, TEXT_EMBEDDINGS_LARGE_3 and three QWEN_1_5B custom variants (one FP8); each repo records a preferredEmbeddingModel and the client can request chunking strategies. AiService adds GetEmbeddings, BulkEmbed, RerankDocuments, RerankResults and ContextReranking, and a tree-sitter based chunker (tree-chunk-napi) is bundled.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Data Plane v2 owns retrieval; the useful part is the per-corpus preferred embedding model and explicit chunking-strategy negotiation.
notes: Quality 4 because: Custom embeddings, reranking and chunking negotiation are strong; retrieval quality is not observable.

name: Git-aware retrieval: PR history search and commit-graph related files
what: The agent can search past pull requests and find files that historically change together with the one being edited.
how: GitIndexService (RepoHistoryInitHandshake, RepoHistorySyncOne, RepoHistorySyncComplete, SearchPRHistory, GetPRIndexingStatus) indexes PR history; GitGraphService (InitGitGraph, BatchedUploadCommitsIntoGitGraph, GetGitGraphRelatedFiles) builds a commit graph. Settings cursor.general.gitGraphIndexing and cursor.semanticSearch.includeCommitsWithFiles and the flag git_snapshot_indexing control them.
verevonRelevance: Co-change and PR-history signals are a cheap way to improve 'what else should I look at' for Verevon's agents working in document or repo Spaces.
notes: Quality 3 because: Only service surfaces and settings were observed; behaviour untraced. Behaviour beyond RPC names and settings was not traced. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): git_snapshot_indexing on.

name: Bugbot: automated pull-request review service
what: A review bot comments on pull requests with bugs it finds, can propose fixes, and learns from reactions; teams choose depth, autofix behaviour and billing.
how: BugbotService (GetEncryptedBugData, AddBugbotFeedback, GetBugBotRunEta, LogDeeplinkEvent), BugbotAdminService (trial controls), AiService.StreamBugBot / StreamBugBotAgentic (SSE and poll variants), CheckBugBotPrice and GetSuggestedBugBotIterations. BugbotMode is DEFAULT, HIGH, AUTO or FRONTIER; BugbotAutofixMode is OFF, MANUAL, AUTO_PR or AUTO_MERGE; BugbotBillingMode is SEAT or TOKEN. BugBotStatus reports iterations, tokens and cost while a run proceeds. Findings are fetched as encrypted bug data and opened from deep links into the editor.
verevonRelevance: A governed review agent with explicit effort tiers, autofix delivery modes (direct push vs side branch) and live cost telemetry is a ready product shape for a Verevon review or QA agent.
notes: Quality 4 because: Product-grade effort tiers, autofix delivery modes and billing; review quality cannot be assessed from the client. Review quality cannot be assessed from the client.

name: Editor-side review: Bugbot subagent, review skill and auto-run on commit
what: Inside the IDE the agent can run a Bugbot-style review of local changes as a subagent, proactively near the end of substantial work, and an auto-run option reviews each commit.
how: A built-in subagent named bugbot is registered with a fixed prompt form (Full Repository Path, Diff kind, Change Description, Custom Instructions) and is single-shot; a security-review subagent is gated to explicit requests. The command cursor.runEditorBugbot is guarded by the feature gates editor_bugbot and bugbot_autorun_killswitch and the user setting autoRunBugbotOnCommit, and references a review-bugbot skill (review-bugbot/SKILL.md) under the flag editor_review_cta_uses_review_bugbot. AiService.StreamDiffReview / StreamDiffReviewByFile provide per-file review.
verevonRelevance: Treating review as a skill plus subagent that the main agent invokes proactively (with kill switches) is a clean way to add review to Verevon's Do mode.
notes: Quality 4 because: Review is integrated into the agent loop with kill switches; the fixed prompt form is rigid but effective. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): editor_bugbot on, bugbot_autorun_killswitch off, editor_review_cta_uses_review_bugbot off.

name: Diff review surface: per-file accept and reject, multi-file inline diffs
what: Agent changes arrive as reviewable diffs with accept and reject controls per hunk or file, a changed-files drawer and keyboard accept-all.
how: Commands composer.accept_all, composer.reject_all, composer.accept_diff_file, composer.acceptComposerStep and cursor.reviewchanges exist; an inline multi-diff editor (cursor.editor.IInlineMultiDiffEditor), cursor.inlineDiff.enablePerformanceProtection and virtualized diff tabs (flag diff_tab_viewport_virtualization) handle large diffs. The Glass window adds tabs for CI, commits and reviews (glass_diff_ci_tab, glass_diff_commits_tab, glass_diff_reviews_tab).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's artifact panel has version diff but no accept/reject per hunk for agent edits; this is the control surface behind trustworthy autonomous edits.
notes: Quality 4 because: Complete accept and reject controls with performance protection; common in IDE agents. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): diff_tab_viewport_virtualization off, glass_diff_ci_tab on, glass_diff_commits_tab on, glass_diff_reviews_tab on.

name: AI code attribution on commits
what: Each commit is scored for how many lines came from Tab, from the agent, or from the human, and the split is reported with line-range annotations.
how: The commits extension runs developer.aiCodeTracking.scoreCommitInternal and AiService.ReportCommitAiAnalytics sends total, tab_lines_added/deleted, composer_lines_added/deleted, non_ai_lines_added/deleted, change_ids, range_annotations and commit source; ReportAiCodeChangeMetrics reports per-change data. The agent also has an ai_attribution tool, and commit/PR attribution messages are part of the request context.
verevonRelevance: Provenance of AI-written content (which paragraph or cell came from which run) fits Verevon's provenance and honesty contracts and could be surfaced per artifact version.
notes: Quality 4 because: Line-level split by source with range annotations is more detailed than peers; upload conditions not confirmed.

name: Best-of-N: parallel attempts with a judge
what: One prompt can be fanned out to several models in parallel, each in its own thread, and the user applies the preferred result while the others are undone.
how: The composer plans fan-out with planBestOfN and runBestOfNFanout; composer data tracks isBestOfNParent, isBestOfNSubcomposer, bestOfNGroupId and helpers that undo other applied siblings. Preferences bestOfNEnsemblePreferences, bestOfNCountPreference and bestOfNDefaultModels exist. AiService.StreamUiBestOfNJudge (SSE and poll) provides a judge, cloud runs carry best_of_n_group_id, and a bestOfNRunner subagent exists; the request origin 'composer-ensemble' and model slug composer-ensemble point to the same feature.
verevonRelevance: Model comparison is a documented Verevon gap; best-of-N with apply-one-undo-others and a judge is a stronger form than side-by-side chat.
notes: Quality 4 because: Fan-out, apply-one-undo-others and a judge are all present; the judge's quality is unknown. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): cloud_agent_best_of_n_disabled off.

name: Commit message, branch name and code-history storytelling
what: The editor drafts commit messages and branch names from diffs, and a subagent writes story-style reports on how code evolved and why.
how: AiService.WriteGitCommitMessage, WriteGitBranchName and TakeNotesOnCommitDiff back the SCM input action (cursor.generateGitCommitMessage). A built-in subagent cursorBlameLearning produces reports on authorship, rationale and tradeoffs using blame data (tool blame_by_file_path; commands cursor.blame and cursor.fileblame).
verevonRelevance: Low-cost features that make agent work legible; the history-narration subagent suits Verevon's document version history.
notes: Quality 3 because: Useful small features with little novelty.

name: Pull-request and CI lifecycle tools for agents
what: Agents can manage PRs end to end: open, label, merge, enable auto-merge, resolve review threads, investigate failed CI checks and babysit a PR until green.
how: Tools include pr_management, edit_pr_labels, set_active_branch, get_pr_code_tour, update_pr_code_tour, record_ci_investigation_findings; BackgroundComposerService exposes MergePullRequest, EnablePullRequestAutoMerge, ReplyToReviewThread, ResolveReviewThread, GetPullRequestDiscussions, CheckPullRequestMergeability, UpdatePullRequestBranch. A ciInvestigator subagent summarises one failing check; the protobuf field babysit_pr_in_cloud_params and simulated-message reason BABYSIT_PR_IN_CLOUD drive cloud babysitting.
verevonRelevance: Not an IDE concern, but 'finish the job after the first answer' (watch a deliverable until it passes a check) is a pattern Verevon scheduled and watch runs lack today.
notes: Quality 4 because: End-to-end PR and CI tooling for agents; depends on the vendor's GitHub integration.

name: Debug mode: hypothesis-driven runtime instrumentation
what: A dedicated mode makes the agent form hypotheses, add logging instrumentation, ask the user to reproduce, then analyse the logs and iterate until the root cause is proven.
how: The Debug mode prompt tells the agent to instrument code and write NDJSON logs either to a file or by POSTing to a local ingest server; the cursor-ndjson-ingest extension binds 127.0.0.1 on ports 7242 to 7942 (ndjson.port, ndjson.bindAddress with a warning about non-localhost) and writes workspace/.cursor/debug.log. A debug subagent with the same method exists and the Delete tool is reserved for clearing logs.
verevonRelevance: A structured 'instrument, reproduce, verify' loop with a local log sink is a reusable pattern for Verevon's computer-use and integration debugging agents.
notes: Quality 4 because: A disciplined hypothesis and log-evidence loop with a local sink; narrow to code debugging.

name: Legacy AI lint and hallucinated-function checks
what: Older AI features check code for bugs, explain lint results and flag calls to functions that do not exist.
how: AiService has StreamAiLintBug, StreamLint, StreamNewLintRule and StreamFixMarkers; LinterService has LintFile, LintChunk, LintFimChunk, LintExplanation and LintExplanation2; HallucinatedFunctionsService exposes a v0ChainRun method. Current use in the agent path is not shown (the agent relies on read_lints instead).
verevonRelevance: Verification of references the model produced (do cited symbols or sources exist) matches Verevon's citation-verification work.
notes: Quality 2 because: Probably vestigial; only service names were seen. Low confidence: only service surfaces were observed; they may be vestigial.

name: Typed agent protocol: server-run loop, client-side execution, three transports
what: The agent loop runs behind one streaming API; the local machine or a cloud VM executes the tools the loop asks for, so the same agent can work against a laptop, a VM or a private worker.
how: agent.v1.AgentService.Run is bidirectional, with RunSSE and RunPoll fallbacks. AgentClientMessage carries run_request, exec_client_message, kv_client_message, conversation_action, interaction_response, client_heartbeat and prewarm_request; AgentServerMessage carries interaction_update, exec_server_message, conversation_checkpoint_update, kv_server_message, interaction_query and ttft_breakdown. ExecServerMessage requests shell, read, write, grep, ls, mcp, fetch, computer_use, record_screen, subagent, hooks and similar operations from the client. A second service, AgentHostService, manages sessions (CreateSession, ForkSession, SendMessage, InterruptTurn, CancelQueuedTurn, RespondToInteraction, AttachSession). The host can choose between the backend loop and a managed local loop behind the gate agent_host_local_loop.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Do loop lives in execution-core with a policy pipeline; a typed bidirectional contract where the loop requests effects from a swappable executor (laptop, VM, broker) is the seam Verevon needs for computer use and per-session sandboxes.
notes: Quality 5 because: A single typed bidirectional contract with executor delegation, three transports and prewarm is the cleanest runtime seam observed. Where the production loop for cloud runs executes is INF (same @anysphere/agent package appears in both client and cloud-agent prompts). Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): agent_host_local_loop off.

name: Eight agent modes with a mode-switch tool and proactive mode nudges
what: Users and the model move between Agent, Ask, Plan, Debug, Multitask, Triage, Project and custom modes; the model can ask to switch and the UI suggests a switch when the prompt looks like another mode.
how: agent.v1.AgentMode lists AGENT, ASK, PLAN, DEBUG, TRIAGE, PROJECT, MULTITASK and CUSTOM; unified chat mode has CHAT, AGENT, EDIT, CUSTOM, PLAN, DEBUG. Mode-specific behaviour is injected as system_reminder blocks (Ask = read-only, Multitask = coordinator, exit reminder when leaving). The switch_mode interaction query lets the model request a switch (user accepts or rejects: composer.plan_mode.switch_to_plan.accept / reject), shift+tab renders Plan or Debug entry points, and composer.suggested_mode_switch.opt_out records user opt-outs. Custom modes (flags custom_agents_enabled, cloud_custom_modes and glass_custom_modes; ManagedSkill can carry a custom_mode) persist in conversation state as durable_custom_mode_id.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has Ask and Do; named modes with their own tool sets and reminders, plus model-initiated mode switches that the user approves, give a cleaner model than a single plan_mode flag.
notes: Quality 4 because: Rich modes with reminders and approved switches; the number of modes adds UX complexity. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): custom_agents_enabled off, cloud_custom_modes off, glass_custom_modes off.

name: Plan mode: plan files, todos and Build in Parallel
what: Plan mode produces a named, editable plan document and a todo list; the user can accept it, edit it, build it, or build it in parallel with async agents.
how: The create_plan tool takes a detailed plan, an optional 3-4 word name (first call only) and todos; the backend writes <name>_<8 hex>.plan.md under the project plans folder with frontmatter (name, overview, todos, isProject) and registers it in a plan registry; project mode can carry phases that flatten into todos. UI events cover plan_created, plan_viewed, plan_manually_edited, plan_accepted, and a Build in Parallel action that injects a system_reminder telling the agent to implement the attached plan, keep todos in progress and not edit the plan file. Plans survive in conversation state (plan, plans map).

name: Plugin bundles: skills, rules, commands, subagents, hooks and MCP in one manifest
what: A plugin is a repository or subfolder that can contribute skills, rules, commands, agents, hooks and MCP servers, installed from GitHub, a git URL or a subdirectory pinned to a commit.

name: Skills: multi-vendor discovery, budgeted catalog, publish as plugin, managed skills

notes: Quality 4 because: A budgeted catalogue and multi-vendor discovery are good; publish flow is strong.

name: Rules system: four rule types, .mdc files, AGENTS.md, team and user rules

name: Hooks: 21 lifecycle events, command and prompt handlers, fail-closed option

name: Cross-vendor compatibility: reads Claude, Codex and agents conventions

Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): enable_cc_plugin_import on, import_3p_plugins on, enable_local_3p_plugin_imports on.

name: Integrations as agent entry points: Slack, Linear, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Jira, Teams, PagerDuty, Sentry

name: Programmatic surfaces: CLI, desktop bridge, SDK origin, webhook API keys

name: Continual learning without a memory store: transcripts as files plus a past-conversation subagent
what: Cloud agents are told to recognise preferences, corrections and tips during a conversation, to ask whether each applies globally or only to the current task, and to rely on a subagent that searches past transcripts in later sessions.
how: The continual_learning prompt section names the past_conversation_explorer subagent, lists signals to recognise (preferences, corrections, tips, codebase knowledge), tells the agent to ask 'always, or just this case?' and to acknowledge briefly that future agents can search transcripts. notes: Quality 4 because: Pragmatic approach, but no automatic memory write was found. No automatic memory write was found in this prompt path; recall depends on later transcript search (INF from prompt text).

name: Conversation search: local SQLite FTS5 index with recency-weighted BM25
what: Users and agents can search all past chats by title, body and branch names, with highlighted snippets and local plus cloud-cached results.
how: A dedicated utility process (conversationSearchMain) keeps a SQLite database with a conversation_fts FTS5 table over title, body and branches (unicode61 tokenizer with diacritics removed, prefix indexes 2 and 3), a reconciliation cursor and an effective conversation cap. Queries combine bm25 column weights (title 1.25, body 1.0) with a recency boost that decays with age, return highlighted title, body snippet and branch matches, and tag results as local or cloud-cache. The search is exposed as an agent tool (search_conversations) and gated by flags (agent_conversation_search_tool, local_agent_transcript_search_in_glass).
verevonRelevance: Server-side chat search is a documented Verevon gap; an FTS index with recency-weighted ranking in a separate process is a small, proven design (Postgres FTS or Tantivy would be the Verevon equivalents).
notes: Quality 4 because: A solid FTS design; local index plus cloud cache. Correction to the scout inventory: aiserver.v1.ConversationsService only has GetCommitMetrics methods and is unrelated to search. REA parsed the file (64,110 AST nodes) but its semantic graph hit the worker heap limit, so all behaviour is read from source. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): agent_conversation_search_tool off, local_agent_transcript_search_in_glass on.

name: Named long-lived agents with a self document, soul file and event subscriptions

notes: Quality 4 because: Persona-as-files with subscriptions is distinctive; gated by flags.

name: Automation memories: per-automation files with optimistic concurrency

name: Model catalogue with lifecycle states, parameterised picker and Max mode

name: Bring your own key, Azure, Bedrock and local provider credentials
what: Users and enterprises can run agents on their own provider accounts, including AWS Bedrock with several credential chains, Azure and API keys, or a local HTTP provider with a key helper script.

name: Prompt and tool variants per model family
what: The system prompt and the tool set differ by model family so each model sees the style it performs best with, including separate prompt versions for Cursor's own models.
how: Prompt sections branch on flags such as isGpt5Family, isGpt55, isGpt56, Codex preamble style, Opus and Sonnet generations and Gemini 3; Cursor models use promptVersion values dsv3-1018, dsv3-1205 and cursor-0226; edit tools vary by vendor (see the edit-tool record) and computer use uses provider-defined tools (Anthropic computer_20250124 at 1280x800, Gemini normalised 0-999 coordinates, OpenAI computer use). what: Requests are built so the provider's prompt cache is reused turn to turn, and caches are warmed while the user is still typing.

The wire protocol has a prewarm_request that mirrors a run request without an action, and AiService/ChatService add WarmComposerCache, KeepComposerCacheWarm, WarmStreamUnifiedChatWithTools, WarmApply and WarmFullFileCmdK. TTFT is measured in segments (server first token, pre-stream setup, provider TTFT, slow-pool wait).
verevonRelevance: Verevon shows cache read tokens already; adding a prewarm call at composer focus and enforcing a stable prefix would reduce first-token latency on every route.
notes: Quality 4 because: Standard techniques (rolling breakpoints, prefix-preserving summaries, prewarm) executed well.

name: Provider-neutral inference layer with executors and request middleware

verevonRelevance: Verevon's Rust inference-core already routes providers; the middleware list (image resize, effort mapping, continuation injection, trailing-empty cleanup) is a checklist of provider quirks to cover.
notes: Quality 4 because: A clean middleware chain; common architecture.

name: Subagent model selection and multi-model ensembles

Video analysis subagents are restricted to Gemini models (gemini-3.1-pro, gemini-3-flash, gemini-2.5-flash).
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs Gemini and DeepSeek providers; routing a modality-specific subagent (video, long context) to the provider that does it best is the way to use them.
notes: Quality 4 because: Per-type override is simple and useful. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): explicit_subagent_models off.

how: AiService.CheckUsageBasedPrice, CheckBugBotPrice and GetEffectiveTokenLimit, flags enable_spend_alerts_percentage_threshold, limit_hit_ui_kill_switch, sand_usage_page and tiered team pricing, and a composer usage summary display setting support this (TeamCreditsService and UsageSimulationService are also defined in the bundle but look like internal admin tooling); composer.model_confirmation_dialog.* guards expensive picks; BugBotStatus streams processed tokens and cost during a run.

notes: Quality 3 because: Surfaces are mostly known from flags and names. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): enable_spend_alerts_percentage_threshold on, limit_hit_ui_kill_switch off, sand_usage_page off.

name: Layered approval modes with a permissions.json and admin override
what: Tool approvals run in one of three modes (ask every time, allowlist, run everything) or an auto-review mode, configured per user, project and admin, with a JSON file for command and MCP allowlists.
how: The shipped schema for .cursor/permissions.json defines mcpAllowlist (server:tool, server:*, *:tool, *:*), terminalAllowlist, approvalMode (allowlist, unrestricted, manual) and autoRun/autoReview allow_instructions and block_instructions (natural-language rules for the classifier). name: Auto-review: a model classifies each risky action as allow or block
what: In auto-review mode a model judges shell, MCP, computer-use, web-fetch and MCP-resource actions; blocked actions return a reason to the agent, which can retry by asking for native approval.
how: A client-side classifier call runs per action with a 10 s timeout and up to 2 attempts, with outcomes allow, block or unspecified (unspecified is retried), fail-safe text 'review manually' on error, an optional shadow mode that classifies without enforcing, and an execution_surface label (host_machine or isolated_box). It is not used for background agents. A block becomes a system reminder telling the agent to retry with requestSmartModeApproval and a smartModeBlockReason so a native approval card is shown; users supply allow and block instructions in permissions.json.
verevonRelevance: A model-based approver with a shadow mode and a human fallback is a practical way to reduce approval fatigue in Verevon's Do mode while keeping the HITL path.
notes: Quality 4 because: A classifier with shadow mode and a fail-safe; not used for background agents. Prompt text of the classifier is server-side and was not observed.

name: Structured shell-command parsing for allowlists and an admin denylist
what: Allowlist matching uses a parsed view of the command (executables, redirects, command substitution) rather than raw prefixes, and admins can deny commands outright.
how: ShellArgs carries simple_commands, has_input_redirect, has_output_redirect and a ShellCommandParsingResult (parsing_failed, executable_commands, has_redirects, has_command_substitution, all_redirects_are_dev_null); allowlist prechecks run before execution for shell, MCP and web fetch, and a hook_approval_requirement and classifier_result can add requirements. admin_command_denylist is pushed in RequestContext and ShellArgs with a kill switch flag.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's risky-tool classifier is a substring list; parsing commands into executables and redirects is the upgrade path for its sandbox terminal.
notes: Quality 4 because: A structured parse result drives allowlists; parser quality not seen. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): admin_command_denylist off.

name: Native sandbox helper with workspace policies and a network proxy
what: Shell commands can run inside an OS sandbox that confines writes to the workspace, restricts reads and routes network traffic through an allow or deny proxy.
how: A Rust helper (cursorsandbox) enforces policies of type workspace_readwrite, workspace_readonly or insecure_none with read boundaries, extra read-only and read-write paths and an optional tmp write block; it runs a built-in HTTP CONNECT and SOCKS5 proxy with allow, deny and logging rules (network_policy version 1, strict mode, capture_denies). A flag sandbox_force_disable_win32 falls back to on. Support is detected per platform: macOS is supported, Linux needs a kernel preflight, and on Windows the helper is proxy-only with no filesystem isolation (isSandboxHelperSupported returns false). Policies are written as JSON files (mode 0700 directory) under ~/.cursor/sandbox-policies, or CURSOR_SANDBOX_POLICY_DIR, with a one-hour cleanup (mcp.js:3509), and caches (npm, pnpm, Go, Cargo, pip, uv) are redirected to temp directories.
evidence: APP:resources/helpers/cursorsandbox.exe (3.5 MB Rust helper; printable strings in scratchpad/tmp/cursor-h/cursorsandbox.strings.txt)
verevonRelevance: Verevon's sandbox is bwrap inside execution-core; the policy shape (read boundary, extra paths, proxy-enforced network policy) is directly portable to its Rust sandbox seam.
notes: Quality 4 because: A good policy model; Windows has no filesystem isolation. Windows has no filesystem sandbox, so an agent running on this audit machine's platform has only network policy. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): sandbox_force_disable_win32 on.

name: Protected paths inside a writable workspace
what: Even when the sandbox allows writes in the workspace, files that could escalate privileges stay read-only for the agent.
how: A hard-coded deny list protects .cursor/*.json, .cursor/**/*.json, .workspace-trusted, cli.json, cli-config.json, mcp.json, mcp-approvals.json, permissions.json, .vscode, .idea, .venv, *.code-workspace, .cursorignore, .claude/*.json, .git/hooks, .git/config, .git/config.worktree, .git/info/attributes and worktree .git pointers, plus system CA bundles and the sandbox-policies folder; rules, commands, skills, agents and worktrees folders under .cursor are explicitly excluded from protection so the agent can author them.
verevonRelevance: A concrete list of the files an agent must never rewrite (approval stores, hooks, git config, workspace tasks) is directly reusable for Verevon's per-session sandbox and Space workspaces.
notes: Quality 5 because: A concrete, well-chosen deny list that closes privilege-escalation routes.

name: Model-requested permission escalation for single commands
what: When a command needs more than the sandbox grants, the model asks for exactly that capability in the tool call (for example full network), which triggers an approval.
how: The shell tool schema has an optional required_permissions array: read-only shells may request network, strict mode allows full_network or all (one item), default allows git_write, full_network, network or all. The prompt tells the model which domains the sandbox already allows (package managers and version control hosts) so it only requests extra access for other domains; SandboxPolicy.allowlist_escalated records approved escalations.
verevonRelevance: Per-command, least-privilege escalation requests give Verevon a precise approval card ('allow network for this command') instead of a blanket tool approval.
notes: Quality 4 because: Least-privilege escalation requests are rare.

name: Network egress controls for local and cloud agents
what: Local sandbox network policy, MCP server network modes and cloud agent egress can each be allowed, denied or locked by admins.
how: GetTeamAdminSettings includes network_allowlist, network_denylist, cloud_agent_egress_allowlist, mirror_sandbox_allowlist_for_egress, SandNetworkControls (egress_mode, allowlist, locked) and BackgroundAgentSettings.egress_protection_mode with a lock flag; the sandbox ships a default allowlist for package managers and git hosts; MCP stdio servers have their own network modes.
verevonRelevance: A single egress-policy vocabulary across local sandbox, MCP and cloud runs is what Verevon needs to state tenant network guarantees consistently.
notes: Quality 4 because: Consistent vocabulary across local, MCP and cloud with admin locks.

name: Privacy modes with a purpose-by-classification storage matrix
what: Five privacy levels (unspecified, no storage, no training, usage data allowed, usage and codebase training allowed) decide what may be stored, logged or used for training.
how: aiserver.v1.PrivacyMode has UNSPECIFIED, NO_STORAGE, NO_TRAINING, USAGE_DATA_TRAINING_ALLOWED and USAGE_CODEBASE_TRAINING_ALLOWED. A policy function maps (mode, field classification, purpose) to allow or deny: classifications are SAFE, CODE, CREDENTIALS, PATH, PROVIDER_INFO and UNSPECIFIED; purposes are storage for training, logging, usage and unsafe-always-allowed. Modes 0 and 1 allow nothing but SAFE; mode 2 allows paths and provider info for logging and any classified data for usage accounting but never for training; modes 3 and 4 allow storage; credentials and unclassified fields are never storable. A table classifies every protobuf field of the agent protocol (for example workspace paths as PATH, shell commands as CODE).
verevonRelevance: Zero-Data-Retention must propagate in Verevon; a field-level classification table plus a (mode, class, purpose) decision function is the mechanism to prove propagation instead of relying on per-feature checks.
notes: Quality 5 because: An explicit (mode, class, purpose) policy with per-field classification. The numeric modes are read from the switch statement; mode 2 = NO_TRAINING is by enum order.

name: RedactedString: privacy by construction in the agent runtime
what: Sensitive strings are wrapped in a type that refuses implicit serialisation, so a logging or telemetry path cannot leak them by accident.
how: Values are created with a classification and field name; toString, toJSON, valueOf and toPrimitive return a redacted token and log a 'would-be redaction' warning in staged enforcement (tests throw); string methods (trim, slice, lowercase) keep the wrapper; reading the raw value requires unwrap with an explicit purpose. Protobuf messages have 'redacted' variants and the conversation state has a RedactedConversationStateStructure.
verevonRelevance: A tainted-string newtype with explicit unwrap(purpose) is idiomatic in Rust and could enforce Verevon's ZDR rule at compile time across Model Plane crates.
notes: Quality 5 because: A taint type with staged enforcement and test-time throws is unusually rigorous.

name: Privacy mode wiring: header, server attestation and withheld index keys
what: Every request states the privacy mode, the client can ask the server whether it is on a privacy pod, and features that need more data are gated on the mode.
how: Requests set x-ghost-mode (true, false or implicit-false) plus client, team, session and a request-checksum header; AiService.PrivacyCheck returns is_on_privacy_pod and is_ghost_mode_on. The index handshake sends the path-encryption key only when privacy mode is off; telemetry reports skip Sentry events in privacy mode; prompt-quality snapshots upload only for the most permissive mode; edit-history append carries a PrivacyModeStatus (PRIVACY_ENABLED, IMPLICIT_NO_PRIVACY, EXPLICIT_NO_PRIVACY).
verevonRelevance: A client-verifiable 'privacy pod' check (the server confirms the retention mode it honours) is the kind of attestation Verevon's ZDR gate lacks for providers.
notes: Quality 4 because: Header plus attestation RPC; server enforcement is unverifiable from the client. Server-side enforcement cannot be verified from the client; PrivacyCheck only shows the contract.

name: Privacy-preserving codebase index: encrypted paths and admin ignore lists
what: File paths sent to the index are encrypted with a per-repository key, embeddings are obfuscated with a per-repository seed, and admins and users can exclude files and repos.
how: Relative paths are encrypted with AES-256-CTR (scheme plaintext when no key) and only a SHA-256 hash of the key is sent in the handshake; the key itself goes to the server only when privacy mode is off. A per-repo orthogonalTransformSeed is registered (INF: a random rotation applied to vectors). Inputs honour a global ignore list setting, hierarchical .cursorignore with symlink handling (admin CursorIgnoreControls), admin repository allow and block lists (legacy and unified JSON) and codebase_protection policies per plan.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ever indexes user-local content for retrieval, encrypting paths client-side and withholding keys in strict modes is a strong baseline.
notes: Quality 4 because: Path encryption and a withheld key; the seed's purpose is inferred. The role of the orthogonal seed is INF from its name and placement.

name: Secrets in cloud agents: keyrings, redaction and commit scanning
what: Secrets for cloud runs are held in team or personal keyrings with grants, injected as environment variables, redacted in tool output and scanned for in commits.
how: BackgroundComposerService has keyring APIs (Create/List/Rename/DeleteKeyring, Create/Update/RevokeKeyringSecret, Grant/Update/RevokeKeyringPermissions); the prompt describes personal over team precedence, repo-scoped secrets and a 'redacted secret' type that is also scanned in commits; secret values may appear as [REDACTED] in tool output and RequestContextEnv.secret_redaction_enabled turns the feature on; BackgroundAgentSettings.restrict_team_secrets_to_admins restricts who may add team secrets. The agent never edits the secret store through files (the keyring UI flag cloud_agent_keyring_ui gates the UI).
verevonRelevance: A grants-based keyring with output redaction and commit scanning is the pattern for Verevon's per-session secrets; it also avoids secrets living in prompts.
notes: Quality 4 because: Grants-based keyring with redaction; details are server-side. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): cloud_agent_keyring_ui off.

name: Prompt-injection posture: prompt-level cautions and approval gates
what: The agent is told to treat instructions inside tool results and linked content as untrusted and not to act on linked threads unless asked; structural controls come from approvals, allowlists and protected files rather than content filtering.
how: Background-agent prompts include a caution about instructions in tool results, especially web search results, and a rule not to comment on linked Slack, GitHub or Linear items unless explicitly asked; the transcript-based compaction fallback wraps the old conversation in a security note saying it may contain adversarial or prompt-injection content, must be treated as informational context only and that only instructions outside the transcript are authoritative; MCP and shell actions pass through allowlists, the auto-review classifier and hooks (beforeMCPExecution, beforeReadFile); browser access has an origin allowlist. No dedicated injection detector was found, but quarantining replayed transcripts is a pattern worth copying.
verevonRelevance: Cursor relies on structure (approvals, sandbox, protected files) more than classifiers; Verevon's capability-before-dispatch design is stronger, but it should add the same explicit 'untrusted tool output' wording to every loop.
notes: Quality 3 because: Mostly prompt-level cautions; no detector. Absence of a detector is INF from search; not proven.

name: Enterprise admin control plane exposed to the client (GetTeamAdminSettings)
what: Admins govern models, MCP, auto-run, ignore rules, integrations, browser, plugins, extensions, network, deeplinks, attribution, workspace trust, sharing and invites from one settings object that every client enforces.
how: GetTeamAdminSettingsResponse has about 70 fields, including allowed_models, blocked_models, models_auto_only, auto_run_controls, auto_review, cursor_ignore_controls, dot_cursor_protection (defaults to true), allowed_mcp_configuration, mcp_controls, background_agent_settings, cli_settings, local_tool_controls (permission ceiling), prompt, command and generic deeplink controls, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Jira, Slack and Linear integration settings, workspace_trust_controls, browser features and origin allowlist, byok_disabled, shared_conversation_settings, allowed_extensions, extension_signing_settings, extension_install_cooldown_settings, first-party and third-party plugin import controls, network lists, sand action audit settings, remote and local permissions file paths with an override flag, shared canvas settings, enforce_hooks_readiness and llm_gateway. A Windows ADMX template exposes sign-in enforcement, allowed login domains, allowed team and organisation ids, workspace trust, update mode, extension gallery URL and allowed extensions.
verevonRelevance: This list is a requirements checklist for Verevon's org admin surface; the 'permission ceiling' and 'locked' patterns (admin sets a maximum users cannot exceed) are the important design idea.
notes: Quality 5 because: About 70 fields covering nearly every AI control, with locks and ceilings.

name: Browser, link and extension trust controls
what: In-app browsing is limited to an admin-defined origin allowlist, external links go through trust prompts and extensions are signature-verified from trusted publishers.
how: cursor.browserOriginAllowlist.ensurePageOriginAllowed and ensureNavigationAllowed are called by the browser tools; settings linkProtectionTrustedDomains, trustedExtensionPublishers and trustedExtensionAuthAccess govern prompts; an external-scheme confirmation page exists; the flag extension_signature_verification and ExtensionSigningSettings enforce signing, with a signing registry that maps the Cursor marketplace to Open VSX.

notes: Quality 4 because: Standard but thorough. Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): extension_signature_verification off.

name: Audit and execution telemetry surfaces
what: Tool calls, hook runs, sandbox results and classifier calls are recorded as structured events and metrics, and admins can enable action audit logs.
how: AgentEventTracker has methods for tool call start and result, skill use, hook execution, smart-mode classifier calls, shell sandbox results, loop detection, summarisation, MCP tool calls and unfinished todos; ToolCallEventService and ChatRequestEventV2Service receive events; about 219 OTel metric names cover agent, agent_kv and MCP; flags sand_action_audit_logs and customize_hooks_execution_log_detail enable audit-oriented views. The scout inventory notes Sentry is skipped in privacy mode.

Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): sand_action_audit_logs off, customize_hooks_execution_log_detail on.

name: Customer-controlled LLM gateway with per-provider routing
what: Enterprises can point the product at their own LLM gateway so model traffic goes through their endpoints and credentials.
how: LlmGatewaySettings has enabled, endpoints (map), audience, routing (providers map with per-model enabled entries), auth_mode, team_credential_status and credential_source_strategy; ClearTeamLlmGatewayCredential exists; AgentRunRequest.client_llm_gateway_credential carries the credential, and cloud and local agents can use it. A local provider with a base URL and key helper provides the same idea per user.
verevonRelevance: For EU and sovereign customers Verevon's inference-core could expose the same switch: route every call through a customer-owned gateway while keeping tool and policy logic in the Model Plane.
notes: Quality 4 because: Customer-owned gateway routing is a strong enterprise option.

name: Multi-agent synthesis: one subagent per model in separate worktrees, then a merged answer
what: For a prompt run with several models, a coordinating agent spawns one subagent per model, each on its own git worktree and branch, then compares the results and writes a single combined solution instead of picking a winner.
how: The 'Multi-Agent Synthesis Mode' section tells the parent to do no work of its own first, spawn subagents in parallel (one per listed model, duplicates allowed), give each a unique filesystem-safe branch name and a fixed prompt template, require each to use a worktree and report branch and summary, then compare approaches and implement a synthesis in the parent's workspace. It complements best-of-N (apply one, undo others).
verevonRelevance: Synthesising several models' attempts (rather than a judge picking one) is a differentiated use of Verevon's multi-provider routing, especially for research or document tasks where parts can be combined.
notes: Quality 4 because: A novel synthesis strategy; prompt-driven.

name: Cloud agent operating contract: git hygiene, test planning, evidence and final-message rules
what: Cloud agents follow a written contract: plan testing before coding, commit each logical change, never force-push, keep git identity unchanged, record a video walkthrough when possible, and end with a message that suits the originating channel.
how: Prompt sections git branch requirements, final_reminders ('you MUST plan your testing strategy' and record a video walkthrough), testing_directives, final_message_instructions and per-origin variants (Slack, Linear, GitHub, API and SDK get a visible final summary) are rendered from code. Other rules: avoid asking the user questions in background mode, set up missing dependencies yourself, prefer a change with failing tests over no change, and direct credentials requests to the secrets UI.
verevonRelevance: A code-rendered 'definition of done' per execution context is a cheap way to standardise Do-mode outputs and evidence (tests run, recording attached) across Verevon's agents.
notes: Quality 4 because: Well defined; some rules are prompt-only. Line anchors approximate within the prompt-section block 36700 to 37070.

name: Canvases: agent-authored React documents with a host SDK and shareable artifacts
what: The agent can write an interactive canvas (dashboard, diagram, prototype) as a React file that renders in the host with theme-aware components and can be shared by link.
how: Canvases are .canvas.tsx files under the project canvases folder; a canvas server provider type-checks after each edit (TypeScript diagnostics with a bundled tsconfig, jsx react-jsx), builds with esbuild-wasm and exposes appJs plus dataJson; cursor.shareCanvasArtifact publishes with a visibility. The shipped SDK 'cursor/canvas' includes layout and text primitives (Stack, Row, Grid, Card, Table, Stat, Callout, Pill, Code), charts (BarChart, LineChart, PieChart), DiffView and DiffStats, a DAG layout, TodoList, UsageBar, form controls, theme tokens and hooks useHostTheme, useCanvasState and useCanvasAction. A canvas skill delivers the design rules (use theme tokens, no hard-coded colours).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's artifact panel is read-only HTML; a typed component SDK with compile-time diagnostics fed back to the model is a stronger artifact contract than free-form HTML.
notes: Quality 4 because: Typed SDK, compile diagnostics and sharing; React-only. Corrects the scout note that Canvas was unconfirmed: the SDK typings ship in the install.

name: Rich composer context: many attachment kinds as typed context
what: Messages can carry files, folders, code selections, terminals, lint errors, git diffs, commits, PRs, docs, web pages, past chats, rules, commands, images, videos, PDFs, console logs and picked UI elements.
how: ConversationMessage includes attached_code_chunks (with intents such as COMPOSER_FILE, RECENTLY_VIEWED_FILE, OUTLINE, MENTIONED_FILE, CODE_SELECTION, VISIBLE_FILE, TERMINAL_SELECTION and summarisation strategies), codebase_context_chunks, commits, pull_requests, git_diffs, images, attached_folders, lints, docs_references, web_references, external_links, summarized_composers, past_chats, cursor_rules, cursor_commands, notepads, console_logs, ui_element_picked, project_layouts, mcp_descriptors, recently_viewed_files, recent_locations_history, human_changes, context_window_status and todos. Documents and videos have attach limits (documents 10 MB).

notes: Quality 4 because: Comprehensive context kinds with intents.

how: AiService.StreamComposerEnhancer (with SSE and poll variants) and a ComposerEnhancerToolCall type back it; the enhanced text streams into the composer.

notes: Quality 3 because: A common feature.

Voice duplex behaviour was not observed.

name: Image generation, image, PDF and video understanding

how: A generate_image interaction query and AiService.RunGenerateImage back the tool, with model slugs gpt-image-1 and grok-imagine-image-quality in the client; image-resizing middleware prepares attachments; videos upload through signed URLs (flag agent_video_signed_url_uploads); the watchVideo subagent is limited to gemini-3.1-pro, gemini-3-flash and gemini-2.5-flash; a PDF viewer (pdf.js) renders PDFs in tabs.

name: Screen recording and video walkthroughs as evidence
what: Agents record their screen while testing and attach a walkthrough video to the final answer.
how: The record_screen tool (RecordScreenToolCall, exec message record_screen) is used by computer-use and cloud agents; the cloud final-reminders section tells agents to record a video walkthrough of their changes; a video review subagent consumes generated videos.
verevonRelevance: A recorded walkthrough as proof of work is a persuasive output for Verevon's agent results and receipts.
notes: Quality 4 because: An unusual 'proof of work' practice.

name: Web search and fetch tools with approvals and an allowlist precheck
what: The agent searches the web with a server-side search that returns an answer and documents, and fetches pages; the user can approve each web fetch.
how: AiService.RunWebSearch takes search_term, explanation and model_id and returns an answer plus documents; RunWebFetch takes a url; the interaction queries web_search_request_query and web_fetch_request_query surface approvals; RequestContext has web_search_enabled and web_fetch_enabled; an allowlist precheck can apply to web_fetch and the auto-review classifier also covers web_fetch actions.

notes: Quality 3 because: Basic; the approvals are the notable part.

name: Documentation retrieval (@Docs) and deep code search with reflections
what: Users can ask questions against indexed third-party documentation, and a deep search mode retrieves code with precomputed summaries ('reflections').
how: AiService.AvailableDocs and DocumentationQuery (doc_identifier, query, top_k, rerank_results) serve docs retrieval; SearchRepositoryDeepContext takes query, top_k, top_reflections_k, index_ids, use_model_on_files and use_reflections and returns top nodes and scored reflections; the request origin 'deep-search' and tool DEEP_SEARCH exist. A client flag disable_docs_client_usage turns docs off.

Client fallback defaults (flag registry in the Glass bundle, used only when the experiment service is uninitialized or errors; live values come from the server): disable_docs_client_usage on.

name: Built-in browser tab with an MCP server: locks, accessibility snapshots, restricted CDP
what: Agents drive a Cursor-owned browser tab through an MCP server with refs from accessibility snapshots, a lock to prevent user interference, screenshots, and a restricted DevTools protocol escape hatch.
how: The cursor-ide-browser MCP exposes browser_navigate, browser_snapshot (YAML with opaque refs tied to the latest snapshot), browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, browser_drag, browser_mouse_click_xy, browser_take_screenshot, browser_get_bounding_box, browser_highlight, browser_tabs, browser_lock and browser_cdp. Instructions forbid CDP Input.* and deny cookie, storage, permission, download, target-management, filesystem-input and navigation methods; large CDP results are saved to files; tabs carry an ownerAgentId; iframes are not accessible; the agent is told to stop after four failed attempts and report blockers (login, captcha, destructive confirmation) rather than improvise.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Quarry executes proposals; the stop-after-four-failures and blocker-report rules, tab ownership by agent id and denied CDP classes are directly reusable in the browser-grant contract.
notes: Quality 4 because: Careful guardrails; iframes unsupported.

name: Computer-use subagent with provider-specific actions
what: A stateful subagent tests applications with a mouse and keyboard on a computer, using each provider's computer-use format.
how: The computer tool is provider-defined: Anthropic computer_20250124 with display width and height and the computer-use beta header, Gemini computer use with normalised coordinates and OpenAI computer use, mapped to one internal ComputerUseAction; a computerUse subagent with shell, read, grep, glob and computer tools is resumed when reused; flags sand_computer_use_playwright and sand_computer_use_unicode_typing tune it; coordinate mode is set in AgentRunRequest.computer_use_coordinate_mode. The computer_use exec message runs on the client or cloud VM, and VNC components (noVNC, react-vnc) ship for remote desktop views.

name: In-app pull request workspace: threads, checks, stacks and agent comment footers
what: Pull requests open in a tab with discussion threads, reviews, commits, changed-files tree, CI checks with rerun messages, stack navigation and special footers for comments written by Bugbot, automations and the self-driving agent.
how: Glass modules include pr-tab-content, pr-discussion-thread, pr-reviews-panel, pr-commits-panel, pr-changed-files-tree, ci-panel, ci-rerun-failure-message, pr-stack-navigator, pr-cursor-bugbot-comment-footer, pr-cursor-automation-comment-footer, pr-comment-add-to-chat-footer (send a comment to the agent chat) and pr-self-driving-task-details; the data comes from BackgroundComposerService PR APIs (discussions, timeline, review thread resolve, merge, auto-merge).
verevonRelevance: Turning review comments into 'add to chat' actions that feed an agent is the loop between human review and agent follow-up that Verevon's document and ticket workflows could mirror.
notes: Quality 4 because: Deep integration with agent follow-up.

name: Typed client feature-flag registry with fallback defaults and kill switches
what: Every AI capability is behind a named client flag with a built-in fallback value, so features can be staged, experimented on and switched off remotely without a release.
how: The Glass bundle embeds a registry of 641 flags, each declared as {client: true, default: true or false}; 182 default to on and the rest to off. Prefix groups show rollout structure: 111 glass_, 44 sand_ (Grok Bot), 34 cloud_agent_, 18 mcp_, 12 bugbot_, 10 cli_. About 20 are named kill switches (for example bugbot_autorun_killswitch, limit_hit_ui_kill_switch, admin_command_denylist_enforcement_killswitch, keybinding_migration_killswitch). The registry gives fallback values only: checkFeatureGate returns the registry default when the Statsig client is uninitialized or a gate check throws, and local developer overrides with expiry sit above it; live values come from the experiment service, which is not observable here. Some fallback defaults qualify the feature records: for example custom_agents_enabled, agent_goal_continuation, full_self_driving, instant_grep_indexing and extension_signature_verification fall back to off, while editor_bugbot, enable_multitask_mode, enable_grind_mode, context_visualizer, enable_ex_hs and sandbox_force_disable_win32 fall back to on.
verevonRelevance: A typed flag registry with explicit kill switches and documented fallback values is the minimum rollout discipline Verevon needs for features that touch tools, memory and privacy.
notes: Quality 4 because: Explicit registry with fallbacks and kill switches; live values are server-side. Extraction used a regular expression over the minified registry and found 641 entries; defaults are client fallbacks, not live values. Per-record notes cite fallback defaults where flags matter.

name: Origin: an in-development code hosting and review surface (flags only)
what: A set of dormant flags and UI modules suggests Cursor is building its own repository, pull request and app surface called Origin that agents can start from.
how: Flags origin_repos, origin_pull_requests_enabled_in_client, origin_apps_ga, origin_raw_file_links, origin_non_admin_namespace_creation_allowed, enable_origin_research_preview_for_enterprises, use_github_pr_links_in_origin_browse, cloud_agent_origin_repos and marketplace_origin_distribution all fall back to off; BackgroundComposerSource has an ORIGIN value; a Glass module origin-repo-unification-context exists; cursor_com_review_pages and cursor_com_review_redirects point to review pages on the vendor site. No implementation of hosting was observed.
verevonRelevance: If Cursor owns the forge, its agents get a closed loop (code, review, merge); Verevon's analogue is owning the document and ticket Space where agents work, which it already does through Control and Data planes.
notes: Quality 2 because: Inference from dormant flags and module names only. Pure inference from flag and module names; treat as a roadmap signal, not a feature.
